newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Ciech sees IPO price at PLN 13.8-18.0.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Ciech sees IPO price at PLN 13.8-18.0.

text.p: Poland's largest chemicals trader Ciech SA set the issue price of its planned initial public offering at 13.8-18.0 zlotys, a Ciech board member said on Wednesday.

"The issue price is initially set in a range between 13.8 and 18 zlotys and the final price will be set by the management board two days before the subscription," Krzysztof Staniszewski told a news conference.
He said Ciech would issue between seven million and 14,203,984 new shares which it would offer to large institutional investors.

"We expect the large investor tranche will be taken up by both passive and active investors -- large domestic and foreign financial institutions," said Ciech president Zdzislaw Matkiewicz, also present.
He added that the whole new issue, expected to bring between 150 and 250 million zlotys, was already underwritten, but declined to name the underwriters.

The company will also offer 9,270,800 existing shares from a stake of more than 11 million shares currently held by the state treasury, on the Warsaw bourse, probably at a special session, at the same price as the institutional offer.
Staniszewski said Ciech would also issue 3-6 million new shares of the "D" series for its 700 eligible employees at an issue price of five zlotys per share.

"As a company which never was fully owned only by the state treasury, Ciech is not subject to the law on the privatisation of state-owned companies which gives employees 15 percent of shares for free," Staniszewski said.
But he said Ciech had set up a special seven-million-zloty fund from which it would extend loans to its employees to buy shares, which they would not be allowed to sell for one year.
He added that Ciech did not plan to float its stock abroad in the form of Global or American Depositary Receipts.

After the capital rise Ciech will have a total of up to 40 million shares of which roughly 26 percent or 10,525,216 shares will be held by current shareholders and up to 23 percent by retail investors.
Institutional investors will have about 36 percent or 14,203,984 shares and employees up to 15 percent.

The state treasury currently holds 51.2 percent of Ciech with the rest owned by numerous, mostly state-owned companies in the chemical sector. After the capital rise the state will have between 2.5 and 10 percent of Ciech.

Th firm expects that the Polish securities Commission (KPW), which received Ciech's issue prospectus on December 30, will clear the shares for public trade within two months and Ciech will enter the bourse around the end of May.

The company expected to make a 51-million-zloty net profit in 1996 against 50 million zlotys in 1995. Ciech, which ranks among Poland's largest companies in terms of sales, expected sales to rise 15.3 percent in 1996 from $960 million in 1995 and $1.3 billion in 1994.
Matkiewicz said he expected both sales and profits to stay at similar levels in 1997.
